name: pwd
description: Prints the absolute path of the current working directory.

flags.description: Print the logical path, honoring $PWD and symbolic links (the default).
Print the physical path with all symbolic links resolved.

examples.explanation: Shows exactly where you are in the filesystem.
On many distributions /var/run is a symlink to /run. pwd -P resolves the symlink and prints the real physical path.

about: pwd is a shell builtin on bash. The standalone /bin/pwd binary also exists and always prints the physical path. The difference matters only when your path contains symbolic links.
useCases: Confirm your location before running destructive commands.
Capture the current directory in scripts: dir="$(pwd)".
mistakes: Confusing the logical and physical paths when symlinks are involved.
